options.metric: For each calendar year, sum number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed separately, giving annual death counts for the two road-user groups
options.denominator: None; this is a count, not a rate
options.grouping: Calendar year and road-user group (motorist, cyclist)
options.chart_type: Two-series line chart of annual counts
options.reason: Annual death counts are the most direct way to compare the two groups year by year.
options.answer: In recorded NYC crash deaths, motorists exceeded cyclists every year: annual totals ranged from 72 to 139 motorist deaths versus 10 to 31 cyclist deaths, and in 2025 the counts were 81 and 23, respectively.
options.interpretation: For each crash year from 2013 through 2025, this framing sums the motorist-killed and cyclist-killed columns separately across all NYC police-reported crashes, with no borough filter; the chart shows motorist counts above cyclist counts in every year, including 81 versus 23 in 2025. This is a direct and defensible comparison of recorded deaths, rather than a rate. It does not measure risk per resident, trip, or mile traveled, and these records cannot establish why counts differ. The final plan retains all 2,132,218 crashes with dates in 2013–2025: both death columns have 0 missing values, and the selected rows have 0 missing/default dates; the date filter excludes null or out-of-range dates (not counted separately in this scoped check), all years have full observed Jan–Dec date extents, and no outcome rows were dropped or imputed.

options.metric: For each calendar year, the share of the combined motorist and cyclist death count attributable to motorists and to cyclists, calculated separately
options.denominator: For each year, the sum of number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed; the two displayed group shares sum to 100% when this denominator is positive
options.grouping: Calendar year and road-user group (motorist, cyclist)
options.reason: A within-year share comparison makes the relative composition of the two groups comparable across years despite differences in their combined totals.
options.answer: Among motorist-plus-cyclist deaths, the motorist share was 72.6%–90.9% by year and the cyclist share was 9.1%–27.4%; in 2025 the shares were 77.9% and 22.1%, respectively.
options.interpretation: For each crash year from 2013 through 2025, the chart divides each group's summed deaths by that year's combined motorist-and-cyclist death total; motorist shares range from 72.6% to 90.9% and cyclist shares from 9.1% to 27.4% (77.9% and 22.1% in 2025). A 100%-stacked bar is defensible for comparing this within-year composition while making explicit that each year's two shares total 100%. Because the denominator excludes pedestrians and other road users, this does not show either group's share of all traffic deaths or a risk rate. The final plan retains all 2,132,218 crashes with dates in 2013–2025: both summed death columns have 0 missing values and the selected rows have 0 missing/default dates; the date filter excludes null or out-of-range dates (not counted separately in this scoped check), observed date extents span Jan–Dec in every year, and no outcome rows were dropped or imputed.
